title: Video QA and release gates
description: The checks every video passes before release: phone-first review, the contact sheet, audio and caption gates, rights and provenance, the blockers that stop a file, the receipt, and release as the owner's word, on a synthetic 30 second social cut.

chapters.title: Finished is not released
chapters.narration: A render finishing is the start of QA, not the end of the job. This lesson runs a synthetic 30 second social cut for Sample Dental Group through every gate we use. Nothing here is a real client. Momo runs the automatic checks and lays out the review; a person makes every release call. Most of these gates exist because something once slipped through. The order matters: cheap mechanical checks first, the human review last, so people spend their time on judgment.
chapters.visual: A finished render card on the left of a row of seven gates, the release switch at the far right still off.

chapters.title: Phone first
chapters.narration: Every video is judged at phone size first, 390 pixels wide, sound off, then sound on. If the line is unreadable or the logo is a smudge at that size, it fails before anything else is checked. Desktop playback is the secondary check. The contact sheet is exported at the phone aspect so the review sees what the audience sees. A line that needs a second read at phone size gets shortened, not enlarged. Most of the audience never sees the desktop version at all.
chapters.visual: A 390 pixel wide phone frame beside a large desktop frame, the phone frame marked first.

chapters.title: The contact sheet
chapters.narration: A contact sheet is one frame per second laid out in a grid. 30 seconds is 30 frames on one page. It shows dead stretches, repeated shots and the exact second a cut drags. The reviewer marks frames, and each mark maps back to a row in the cut plan. We never review from memory of a playback; we review from the sheet. A dead stretch is usually two seconds of the same frame; the sheet makes it obvious.
chapters.visual: A 30 frame grid with two frames marked and arrows to the cut plan rows they came from.

chapters.title: Audio gates
chapters.narration: Loudness is measured and normalized for the platform. Silence longer than a second is flagged. Voice sits above music by a fixed margin. The track is licensed and the license file is in the inventory. A video with the right picture and the wrong loudness loses to the post before it, so audio is a gate, not a note. The levels are checked on the master, not on the preview, because the preview is encoded differently.
chapters.visual: Loudness meter in range, a flagged one second gap, voice above music by a marked margin, a license file in the inventory.

chapters.title: Captions and text
chapters.narration: Captions are checked word for word against the reviewed script and timed to the audio. On screen text is checked for the banned characters and words in our style, for digits in numbers and for readability at phone size. Every claim in text or voice must be a verified fact. A number nobody can source is removed, not softened. If a word in the captions differs from the script, the caption file is rebuilt from the script, never patched by hand.
chapters.visual: Caption check passing beside an on screen line with a flagged unsourced number struck out.

chapters.title: Rights and provenance
chapters.narration: Every clip, image, font and track has a rights status in the inventory: owned, licensed or missing. Missing blocks release. Generated images are allowed for props and boards, never to depict a client's real staff, office or work. The receipt lists the hash of every input, so provenance is provable later. The inventory is the single place rights live, so nobody has to remember which track was cleared.
chapters.visual: Rights column with owned, licensed and one missing row in red, and a note that generated images are props only.

chapters.title: The blockers list
chapters.narration: Some things fail a video on sight: any generated by or sent from footer, an AI mention in the credits, a real client name in a public repository, a price or date nobody confirmed, a logo on a white box instead of transparent, default interface type in an ad. Momo scans for the mechanical ones. People catch the rest. The scan runs on the captions, the transcript and the end card, since footers hide in all three.
chapters.visual: Six blocker cards in red on paper: footer, AI credit, client name in public, unconfirmed price, logo on a box, interface type.

chapters.title: Hashes and the receipt
chapters.narration: When a video passes, the master, poster, captions and transcript are hashed and written to a receipt with the plan hash and every check result. The receipt travels with the file. If a copy is questioned a month later, we compare hashes and know in seconds whether it is the file we released. The receipt also names the version of the plan and the engine that made the file.
chapters.visual: Receipt card listing four output hashes, the plan hash and the check results, clipped to the video file.

chapters.title: Release is the owner's word
chapters.narration: Passing QA makes a file ready. It does not send it anywhere. Posting, sending to a client or publishing to a site is a separate decision made by the owner, in the right channel, with the receipt attached. Agents stage, draft the note and wait. Merge is not deploy, and ready is not released. A client delivery goes in the client's own channel, with the owner's words, not an agent's.
chapters.visual: A ready folder with a drafted note, and an owner key turning the release switch.

chapters.title: Make the gate, not the fix
chapters.narration: When a video fails for a reason we have seen before, we add the check, not just the fix. The black frame detector exists because of one dark shot. The footer scan exists because of one slip. The gates in this lesson are the memory of every miss. Keep adding to them, and the stack gets safer every week. A gate that fires wrong gets fixed, not removed.
chapters.visual: A gate row growing by one new card, with the dark shot and the footer slip shown as the reasons behind two older gates.
